questions.q: On which continent is the Andes mountain range located, and what is its primary spatial orientation?
questions.a: The Andes mountain range is located in South America along its western coast, running in a predominantly north-south orientation. A wrong answer (e.g., choosing North America or an east-west orientation) reveals that the student is confusing the Andes with the Rockies or Himalayas due to a lack of continent-to-landform spatial mapping.

questions.q: Why do geographers classify the Himalayas as the "highest" mountain range while classifying the Andes as the "longest" mountain range on land?
questions.a: The Himalayas contain the world's highest peaks measured by height above sea level (including Mount Everest at 8,848+ meters), but cover a continuous distance of about 2,400 km. The Andes have lower maximum peak heights (Aconcagua at ~6,961 meters), but extend over approximately 7,000 km from north to south, making them much longer in distance. A wrong answer showing confusion between height and length indicates the student treats all "large" landform measurements as identical.

questions.q: A geographer tracks two air masses: Mass A moves eastwards hitting an east-west aligned range in Europe (the Alps), while Mass B moves eastwards across North America hitting a north-south aligned range (the Rockies). Which mountain range acts as a continuous long wall blocking east-west moving moisture over several thousand kilometers from north to south?
questions.a: The Rockies act as a continuous north-south wall across North America, blocking moist air moving inland from the Pacific Ocean across many degrees of latitude. Steps: 1. Determine orientation of Rockies (north-south along western North America). 2. Determine orientation of Alps (arc shaping east-west across southern Europe). 3. Compare blocking profile against east-moving air: A north-south wall creates a broad barrier to west-to-east moving winds. A wrong answer selecting the Alps reveals an inability to visualize how line orientation (north-south vs east-west) interacts with wind movement patterns.

questions.q: Compare the physical location and orientation of the Alps in Europe with the Himalayas in Asia. What primary similarity do they share in their spatial alignment?
questions.a: Both the Alps and the Himalayas share a predominantly east-west orientation across their respective continents (southern Europe and southern Asia), acting as northern or central latitude barriers. A wrong answer stating they run north-south shows a failure to read directional trends on physical map projections.

questions.q: A student claims: "Because Mount Everest is in Asia, the Himalayas must be both the highest and the longest mountain chain on Earth." Critique this statement using geographical facts.
questions.a: The statement is false. While the Himalayas are indeed the highest mountain range containing Mount Everest, the longest continental mountain range on Earth is the Andes in South America (~7,000 km continuous chain), whereas the Himalayas span about 2,400 km. A wrong answer accepting the student's claim shows an error where a single extreme property (highest peak) is incorrectly generalized to all dimensions of a geographical feature.

questions.q: Design a summary key for a world physical atlas that categorizes the four major mountain ranges (Himalayas, Andes, Rockies, Alps) based on two criteria: Continent and Primary Alignment Trend (North-South or East-West).
questions.a:
A complete answer must organize the four ranges accurately:
1. Himalayas: Asia | East-West alignment
2. Alps: Europe | East-West alignment
3. Andes: South America | North-South alignment
4. Rockies: North America | North-South alignment
A poor answer will misplace continents (e.g., swapping Andes and Rockies) or confuse vertical versus horizontal alignment on the world map.

questions.q: Fill in the blank: Mountain ranges are major ______ chains of mountains formed primarily through tectonic activity, spanning vast stretches of land across continents.
Fill in the blank: When you look at photos of snow-covered peaks like Kanchenjunga or Mount Everest, you are looking at the ______, India's northern mountain wall.
What is Mountain ranges? State the definition given in this lesson.
questions.a: Mountain ranges are major continuous chains of mountains formed primarily through tectonic activity, spanning vast stretches of land across continents.

questions.q: What common mix-up does this lesson flag about Mountain ranges?
questions.a: Students frequently confuse the Andes and the Rockies regarding which continent each belongs to, and mistakenly assume that the Himalayas are the longest mountain range in the world because they contain Mount Everest (the highest peak).

questions.q: What must you be able to do to master this topic?
questions.a: Students can identify, locate, and differentiate the Himalayas, Andes, Rockies, and Alps on a world physical map, state their respective continents and spatial orientations (east-west vs north-south), and compare their relative length and elevation characteristics.
